title: entity history behind its guards — `mask unless` field DROPPED from the trail, `auditable`/`versioned` stamps kept out of the diff, an inherited read gate + a `requires`-gated op (403 via the authz ladder), and an unaudited sibling with no history route
note: split from `audit-history` (auth-less, so it can pose none of these) rather than widening it, so that golden stays the reviewed answer key it is; the refused side of every gate is AUTHZ_LADDERS["audit-history-guarded"]

authzGate.//: The history read behind its guards.  Employee's reads are UNGATED, so the mask is their only authz surface; the ladder reads Employee's history with both principals and the golden pins the two bodies (salary's entries kept for `ops.manage`, dropped for `ops.none`) — the mask's witness, as a body and not a status.  Payslip's gated reads are refused by the ladder; only its by-id read (ungated, masked) is pinned.

//: Entity history behind its guards (audit-history-guarded.ddd) — the half of each guard the fixture's `test e2e` cannot pose, because the e2e has one principal and it passes every gate and the mask.

1. THE MASK, unprivileged side.  Employee's reads are ungated, so the unauthorized principal (`permissions: ["ops.none"]`) reads the SAME trail as the authorized one (`ops.manage`) and both bodies are recorded.  The seed creates a row and raises its salary, so the trail is `create` + `raise`: the authorized body carries `salary` in both entries, the unauthorized body has `salary` DROPPED from the create and the raise entry's `changes` EMPTY.  A backend that redacted (`before: null, after: null`) instead of dropping, or that keyed the mask on "is there a principal" rather than the permission, differs here. 2. THE GATED OPERATION — 403 / 204. 3. THE INHERITED GATE.  `Payslip`'s history read has no `requires` of its own; it inherits the list read's.  A backend that served history through a path that skipped the inherited gate answers 200 where the list answers 403.  The ABSENT-id arm is the ordering witness: the gate runs before the row lookup, so the unauthorized caller gets 403 — not a 404 that would confirm the row does not exist — while the authorized caller gets the 404. 4. NO ROUTE.  `Desk` is not audited, so its `/{id}/history` is the framework's route-miss 404 for both principals — a backend that emitted the route for every aggregate (an empty `[]`) differs here.

gated.label: masked field — ungated history, both principals read it
gated operation — the one a workflow also calls inline
inherited gate — the gated list read
inherited gate — an ABSENT row's history: the gate runs first
